name: Synopsys
subcategory: Full-flow EDA, silicon IP and simulation
role: Makes the synthesis, place-and-route, verification and signoff software that turns the code describing an AI accelerator's logic (its RTL) into a layout a fab can build. It also sells the largest commercial catalog of silicon IP, ready-made circuit blocks that chip designers license. Its 2025 acquisition of Ansys added multiphysics simulation for thermal and power integrity.
shareNote: About $8 billion of calendar 2025 EDA and IP revenue including Ansys, against Cadence at $5.30 billion and Siemens EDA at an estimated $2.2 billion to $2.5 billion
aiRelevance: Every leading-edge AI accelerator is designed and checked with a full set of electronic design automation (EDA) tools before it goes to the fab. Synopsys supplies the largest single share of those tools.

revenue.basis: Total revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Cadence Design Systems
subcategory: Digital and analog implementation, verification, IP
role: The second-largest of the three main makers of chip design (EDA) software, strong in analog and custom design, simulation and hardware emulation. Designers verify large AI chips on its Palladium and Protium emulation systems, which run a design in hardware before it goes to the fab.
shareNote: About $5.30 billion of calendar 2025 EDA revenue, second behind Synopsys
aiRelevance: Emulation capacity is one of the limits on AI chip schedules, and Cadence is one of two credible suppliers.

revenue.basis: Total revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Siemens EDA
subcategory: Design for test, physical verification, Calibre
ownership: Subsidiary of Siemens AG of Germany (acquired as Mentor Graphics in 2017)
role: The third-largest maker of chip design (EDA) software. Its Calibre tool is the de facto standard for physical verification, the check foundries use to confirm a layout follows their manufacturing rules before they accept it. It also sells design-for-test software. Foundries write the rule files they give chip designers in Calibre's format.
shareNote: Estimated $2.2 billion to $2.5 billion of calendar 2025 EDA revenue, third behind Synopsys and Cadence. The EDA country share counts it under Germany, its parent's home
aiRelevance: TSMC requires a layout to pass Calibre's checks with no errors before it will make the chip, and Samsung and Intel do the same.

name: Ansys
subcategory: Multiphysics, thermal and power integrity simulation
ownership: Subsidiary of Synopsys since the acquisition closed in 2025
role: Makes the thermal, electromagnetic and structural simulation software used to model how a 1 kW accelerator package heats, warps and delivers power. Its RedHawk tool is the standard for power integrity signoff, the final check that power reaches every part of a chip as designed.
aiRelevance: Heat and warpage are the limiting design problems for kilowatt-class packages and liquid-cooled racks, and Ansys software simulates both.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated, US GAAP
revenue.note: Ansys has filed no accounts since Synopsys bought it in July 2025, so this is its last annual figure.

name: Empyrean Technology
subcategory: Analog and flat-panel EDA, China domestic substitution
ownership: Public, with state-linked shareholders including China Electronics Corporation
role: A Chinese EDA vendor. In its 2025 annual report, filed in April 2026, it says it has complete design tool chains for analog, memory, radio-frequency and flat-panel display circuits. The same report says its digital tools cover 80 percent of the main tools for digital design. It is the main company in China's effort to replace the American EDA tools that export controls can cut off.
aiRelevance: To design advanced AI chips without US software, China has to finish Empyrean's tool chain.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Primarius Technologies
subcategory: Device modeling, SPICE simulation and DTCO
role: A Chinese EDA vendor that makes device modeling, parameter extraction and fast SPICE circuit simulation software. Device models describe how the transistors on a foundry's process behave, so chip designers can simulate their circuits on that process.
aiRelevance: A Chinese AI chip designer cut off from foreign tools needs device models first.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Semitronix
role: Supplies test-chip design software, on-wafer electrical test systems and yield analysis tools used to measure and debug a new manufacturing process. Its products fall between design software and metrology (measurement) equipment.
aiRelevance: Whether a Chinese fab can build AI logic economically depends on yield learning, the work of raising the share of good chips on each wafer.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Arm Holdings
subcategory: CPU instruction set and core IP
ownership: Public, majority owned by SoftBank Group
role: Licenses the CPU architecture and cores used in the host processors that feed data to AI accelerators. These include Nvidia's Grace and Vera CPUs and the Arm cores inside the server chips that large cloud companies design. It also licenses the interconnect and system IP around them. In 2026 it launched the Arm AGI CPU, its first production chip. By May 2026, ASRock, Lenovo, Quanta and Supermicro were taking orders for servers built on it.
aiRelevance: The CPUs in Nvidia's Grace and Vera platforms and in large cloud companies' server chips use the Arm architecture, so building them requires a license from Arm.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated income statements, US GAAP

name: Rambus
role: Licenses the memory controller and interface (PHY) IP that connects a processor to DDR5, LPDDR and HBM memory. It also sells register clock drivers, the buffer chips on server memory modules.
aiRelevance: HBM and high-capacity server DRAM interfaces are among the hardest blocks to design, and Rambus is one of the few sources of proven IP.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Alphawave Semi
subcategory: High-speed SerDes and chiplet connectivity IP
ownership: Acquired by Qualcomm in a deal announced in 2025 and no longer separately listed
role: Supplies multi-gigabit connection IP (SerDes, PCIe, UCIe and Ethernet) that moves data between chiplets and between accelerators. Qualcomm bought it to build data-center silicon.
aiRelevance: The quality of SerDes IP sets how much bandwidth an AI system can reach between dies and across a rack.

revenue.basis: Revenue, continuing operations, consolidated statement of comprehensive income, UK-adopted IFRS
revenue.note: Alphawave is now part of Qualcomm. The figure comes from its 2025 accounts filed at Companies House.

name: SiFive
role: Sells RISC-V CPU cores, including vector and matrix cores used as control processors inside AI accelerators. RISC-V is the license-free alternative to Arm, and Chinese chip designers are adopting it heavily.
aiRelevance: Most AI accelerators need embedded control cores, and RISC-V avoids both Arm royalties and US-UK licensing exposure.

name: Imagination Technologies
ownership: Private, owned by Canyon Bridge Capital Partners
role: Licenses GPU and neural network accelerator IP for edge and automotive silicon. Its ownership by a China-linked fund made it an early test case for technology transfer scrutiny in the UK.
aiRelevance: Supplies inference GPU IP for edge devices.

name: Nvidia
subcategory: Merchant GPUs and rack-scale AI systems
role: Designs the Blackwell and Rubin GPUs, the NVLink connections that join many GPUs into one system, and the NVL72 rack systems. Most AI training and a large share of inference run on this hardware. It also makes the CUDA software stack that ties developers to its hardware.
aiRelevance: Suppliers across the chain plan around Nvidia's demand, from bookings for TSMC's CoWoS packaging to HBM memory allocation to queues for power-grid connections.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: AMD
subcategory: Merchant GPUs, server CPUs and rack systems
role: Designs the Instinct MI355X and MI400 accelerators and EPYC server CPUs. Since buying ZT Systems in 2025 it also designs rack-scale AI systems. It is the only company other than Nvidia that sells AI accelerators on the open market at scale.
aiRelevance: AMD is the main competitive check on Nvidia's pricing, and most large buyers are qualifying it as a second source.

revenue.basis: Net revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Intel
ownership: Public, and the US government took a large equity stake in 2025
role: Designs Xeon server CPUs and the Gaudi accelerator line. Xeon chips are still the host CPUs in most AI clusters. Its product business is separate from Intel Foundry, the company's manufacturing arm.
aiRelevance: Xeon remains the default host CPU in AI servers, even where the accelerators come from another company.

revenue.basis: Net revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Google
role: Designs the Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), and announced the eighth generation, the TPU 8t and TPU 8i, in April 2026. It uses TPUs in its own data centers and offers them to cloud customers. Broadcom and MediaTek work with it on the physical design, which turns a chip design into a layout, and on manufacturing at TSMC.
aiRelevance: TPUs give Google a large AI training fleet that does not depend on Nvidia, and other large cloud companies have followed with chips of their own.

name: Annapurna Labs
subcategory: Hyperscaler in-house training and inference silicon
role: Amazon's chip design arm. It designs the Trainium training chips, Inferentia inference chips and the Nitro data processing units used across AWS. Trainium 3 is the current generation.
aiRelevance: Trainium is Amazon's in-house alternative to Nvidia in its own cloud, and Amazon builds its capacity plans around it.

name: Microsoft Azure Silicon
role: Designs the Maia accelerator family and the Cobalt Arm server CPU for Microsoft's Azure cloud. It also designs the 'sidekick' racks that sit beside the servers and supply the liquid cooling they need. Maia 200 is the current generation.
aiRelevance: Maia gives Microsoft its own chip for its inference work, so it can depend less on Nvidia's pricing and allocation.

name: Meta Platforms
role: Designs the MTIA inference accelerator for its recommendation and ranking workloads, built with Broadcom at TSMC. Meta is also one of the largest buyers of GPUs from outside chip vendors.
aiRelevance: MTIA shows how much inference work a single app company can move off outside vendors' GPUs and onto its own chip.

name: Broadcom
subcategory: Custom AI ASICs (XPUs) plus Ethernet switch silicon
role: Co-designs and supplies the custom AI accelerators used by Google, Meta and other hyperscalers. It is also a leading seller of Ethernet switch chips, including its Tomahawk and Jericho lines, and it supplies the PCIe and SerDes IP that connect AI clusters.
aiRelevance: Broadcom designs custom accelerators and also supplies the Ethernet networking chips that connect them in an AI cluster.

revenue.basis: Total net revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Marvell Technology
subcategory: Custom AI silicon, optical DSPs and interconnect
role: Designs custom AI accelerators and infrastructure chips for hyperscalers, plus networking chips such as optical DSPs, retimers and Ethernet controllers for AI clusters. It ranks second to Broadcom in custom AI chips and competes with it directly to design hyperscalers' accelerators.
aiRelevance: Marvell is the credible second source for hyperscalers that do not want Broadcom to hold every custom silicon program.

revenue.basis: Net revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Alchip Technologies
subcategory: ASIC design services and backend implementation
role: A design services firm that takes a customer's AI accelerator design through physical layout, tape-out and supply at TSMC, including 2.5D packaging. It is one of the few firms with production experience on reticle-limit AI dies, the largest chips a lithography tool can print in one exposure.
aiRelevance: Design service capacity on advanced nodes is scarce, and Alchip is one of the handful of firms that can deliver an AI chip in TSMC's CoWoS packaging.

revenue.basis: Operating revenue, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: Global Unichip
ownership: Public, with TSMC as the largest shareholder
role: TSMC's design services affiliate. It does the physical design and IP integration for customers' custom AI chips (ASICs) and delivers the finished chips, made on TSMC processes and packaging. Its ties to TSMC give it early access to new processes.
aiRelevance: Global Unichip is the fastest route from an AI chip design to a finished chip on a leading-edge TSMC process with CoWoS packaging.

revenue.basis: Net revenue, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: MediaTek
role: Best known for its smartphone chips, MediaTek also designs custom AI chips (ASICs) and works on Google's TPU program. It has experience designing high-volume chips on advanced nodes.
aiRelevance: MediaTek is the third credible custom AI silicon partner alongside Broadcom and Marvell.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: Qualcomm
subcategory: Edge AI SoCs and data-center inference accelerators
role: Designs Snapdragon chips with built-in neural engines that run AI on phones and other devices. In 2025 it announced the AI200 and AI250 rack-scale inference accelerators. Its purchase of Alphawave added the high-speed connection (SerDes) IP a data-center chip needs.
aiRelevance: Qualcomm is targeting inference, the running of trained models, where memory capacity per dollar matters more than the peak compute that training needs.

revenue.basis: Total revenues, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Cerebras Systems
role: Builds the Wafer Scale Engine, a single processor that covers almost an entire 300 mm wafer. It keeps its memory on the chip as SRAM instead of using separate HBM stacks. It sells systems and inference cloud capacity.
aiRelevance: Wafer-scale integration needs neither HBM nor advanced packaging capacity, the two tightest constraints in the chain.

revenue.basis: Total revenue, consolidated, US GAAP
revenue.note: Cerebras listed in May 2026, so the figure comes from its listing prospectus.

name: Groq
ownership: Private, venture-backed, and licensed its inference technology to Nvidia on a non-exclusive basis in December 2025
role: Designs the Language Processing Unit (LPU), an inference chip that uses large on-chip SRAM and no HBM, and whose compiler schedules every operation in advance. It sells few chips. Instead it runs AI models in its own cloud and charges customers per token of text processed.
aiRelevance: An SRAM-only design needs no HBM, the scarcest input in the AI chain.

name: HiSilicon
role: Huawei's chip design arm. It designs the Ascend 910C and the announced 950 and 960 accelerators. SMIC makes its chips without EUV lithography tools, and that limits yield and volume.
aiRelevance: Ascend is the main measure of how far China has gone in replacing foreign AI accelerators with its own.

name: Cambricon Technologies
subcategory: Merchant AI training and inference chips
ownership: Public (Shanghai STAR Market), with state-linked shareholders
role: Designs the Siyuan training and inference accelerators and sells them to Chinese cloud operators. Among listed Chinese companies that design AI chips for sale to other firms, it is the largest. It is on the US Entity List, which restricts US exports to it, and has its chips made in China.
aiRelevance: Cambricon is the main listed company tied to China's shift to domestic AI accelerators, and its revenue tracks how many are deployed.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Hygon Information Technology
subcategory: x86 server CPUs and DCU accelerators
ownership: Public (Shanghai STAR Market), state-linked, and its planned merger with Sugon was terminated in December 2025
role: Makes x86-compatible server CPUs, derived from an AMD license, and the Deep Computing Unit (DCU) accelerator line. It supplies Chinese government and state enterprise data centers.
aiRelevance: Hygon supplies the domestic host CPUs that Chinese AI clusters need alongside domestic accelerators.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Moore Threads
subcategory: General-purpose GPUs for graphics and AI
ownership: Public (Shanghai STAR Market), on the US Entity List
role: Builds full-function GPUs with a CUDA-like software layer, aimed at replacing Nvidia in Chinese workstations and training clusters. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market after being placed on the US Entity List.
aiRelevance: Moore Threads is one of the Chinese firms trying to build a general-purpose GPU, for graphics as well as AI.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Biren Technology
ownership: Public (Hong Kong), on the US Entity List
role: Designs the BR100 series general-purpose GPUs for AI training and high-performance computing. Export controls forced it to redesign its chips so they no longer use TSMC's most advanced processes.
aiRelevance: Biren is one of the few Chinese firms attempting a full training-class GPU.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statement of comprehensive loss, IFRS Accounting Standards; table in RMB thousands

name: MetaX
role: A Chinese designer of general-purpose GPUs, whose Xiyun and Xisi lines are built for AI training and inference in Chinese data centers. It offers a CUDA-compatible software stack.
aiRelevance: One of the Chinese GPU startups that listed in 2025 and 2026 to fund domestic AI silicon.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Iluvatar CoreX
subcategory: GPGPU for AI training and inference
role: Designs the Tiangai and Zhikai general-purpose AI accelerators for Chinese data centers, built to work with mainstream AI frameworks.
aiRelevance: A domestic vendor competing for the Chinese training market that Nvidia can no longer serve.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statement of profit or loss and other comprehensive income, HKFRS Accounting Standards; table in RMB thousands

name: Tenstorrent
subcategory: RISC-V AI processors and licensable IP
ownership: Private, with investors including Samsung, Hyundai and LG
role: Builds AI accelerators around RISC-V cores, with Ethernet links that join many chips into one system. It also licenses the designs as IP so customers can build their own chips.
aiRelevance: Licensable AI IP lets countries and companies build accelerators they control without designing one from scratch.

name: SambaNova Systems
role: Builds reconfigurable dataflow units, AI chips that are set up to match how data flows through each model. They use a large three-tier memory system. SambaNova sells them as an inference cloud service and as full systems for companies that want to run models on their own premises.
aiRelevance: Dataflow chips give up some flexibility to keep more of their hardware busy when running transformers, the model design behind large language models.

name: d-Matrix
role: Builds inference accelerators that compute inside SRAM, which cuts the energy spent moving model weights. They are aimed at batch inference, which runs many requests to a large language model at once.
aiRelevance: In-memory compute cuts the data movement between memory and processor that makes inference expensive.

name: Etched
role: Designing Sohu, a custom chip (ASIC) that hard-wires the transformer architecture into silicon. The transformer is the model design behind large language models. Sohu gives up flexibility to do more work per watt.
aiRelevance: A bet that AI models will keep using the transformer design long enough to justify fixing it in hardware.

name: Rebellions
ownership: Private, merged with SK Telecom's Sapeon in 2024, with SK Group and Arm as investors
role: An AI chip startup building the Rebel inference accelerator with Samsung Foundry and SK hynix HBM. It is the national champion for Korean AI silicon.
aiRelevance: Rebellions is a test of whether Korea's strength in memory chips can extend to designing AI accelerators.

name: FuriosaAI
role: Builds the RNGD inference accelerator, which uses HBM3 memory and an architecture designed around tensor contraction, the core math of AI models. It is aimed at companies running inference where power is limited. It turned down an acquisition offer from Meta in 2025.
aiRelevance: One of the few startups outside the US shipping an inference chip with HBM in production.

name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
subcategory: 300 mm polished and epitaxial wafers, photoresist, pellicles
role: The world's largest silicon wafer maker by capacity and shipments. Silicon wafers are the blank discs every logic and memory die is built on. Shin-Etsu held an estimated 22 percent of global 300 mm wafer capacity at the end of 2024, according to the October 2025 listing prospectus of the Chinese wafer maker Eswin. It also makes ArF and EUV photoresist, the light-sensitive coating chip patterns are printed into, and pellicles, the thin films that keep dust off photomasks. So it supplies three separate stages of the chain.
aiRelevance: Leading-edge AI logic requires epitaxial 300 mm wafers with defect densities only a handful of firms can reach. An epitaxial wafer carries an extra layer of pure crystal grown on its surface.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, J-GAAP

name: SUMCO
role: The second-largest silicon wafer maker by capacity and shipments. It makes only wafers, selling polished and epitaxial 300 mm wafers to logic and memory fabs worldwide. It held an estimated 20 percent of global 300 mm wafer capacity at the end of 2024, according to Eswin's October 2025 listing prospectus. New capacity takes three to four years to add, and customers contract for it years ahead.
aiRelevance: Wafer supply is the first physical limit on how many AI dies can be made. The top five wafer makers served around 75 percent of the market in 2025.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, J-GAAP

name: GlobalWafers
subcategory: Silicon wafers, SOI and compound substrates
ownership: Public, controlled by Sino-American Silicon Products
role: The third-largest wafer maker, with fabs in Taiwan, Japan, the US and Europe. It built a new 300 mm plant in Sherman, Texas, with CHIPS Act support. In its annual report for 2025 it ranked itself third and put its shipments at about 15 to 20 percent of global semiconductor wafer output. It also supplies silicon-on-insulator (SOI) and compound semiconductor substrates.
aiRelevance: The main non-Japanese source of leading-edge wafers and the one adding capacity inside the United States.

revenue.basis: Operating revenue, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: Siltronic
ownership: Public, with Wacker Chemie holding a large minority stake
role: Europe's silicon wafer maker, with 300 mm capacity in Germany and a newer fab in Singapore. Its planned sale to GlobalWafers lapsed in 2022 when the German government did not grant investment clearance before the deadline.
aiRelevance: One of the top five wafer makers, which served around 75 percent of the market in 2025, and the only European one among them.

revenue.basis: Sales, consolidated statement of profit or loss, IFRS

name: SK Siltron
subcategory: 300 mm silicon wafers and SiC substrates
ownership: Part of SK Group, which agreed in July 2026 to sell a 70.6 percent stake to Doosan
role: Korea's silicon wafer maker, supplying 300 mm wafers largely to Samsung and SK hynix. It also makes silicon carbide substrates for power devices at a US plant in Michigan.
aiRelevance: Supplies the wafer substrate for a large share of the world's DRAM and HBM output.

name: Soitec
role: Makes engineered substrates with its Smart Cut process, which moves a thin crystal layer from one wafer onto another. Most are silicon-on-insulator for radio-frequency (RF) and automotive chips, or piezoelectric-on-insulator for radio filters.
aiRelevance: Its substrates go into some of the RF and edge chips around AI systems.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated income statement, IFRS

name: National Silicon Industry Group
ownership: Public (Shanghai STAR Market) and state-backed, with the National IC Fund as an investor
role: China's state-backed silicon wafer group, which owns Shanghai Zing Semiconductor (300 mm wafers) and Okmetic in Finland (specialty wafers). It is China's domestic alternative to Japanese wafer supply.
aiRelevance: A Chinese supply chain that does not depend on Japanese exports needs domestic wafer supply first.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Hemlock Semiconductor
ownership: Private, majority owned by Corning with Japanese partners
role: Makes the ultra-pure polysilicon that is melted to grow the crystal ingots wafers are cut from. Only a few plants worldwide make semiconductor-grade material. Siltronic names Hemlock among the five major suppliers of electronic-grade silicon in 2025.
aiRelevance: Every wafer in every AI chip starts as polysilicon from one of a handful of qualified plants.

name: Wacker Chemie
role: One of the few producers of semiconductor-grade polysilicon, which it makes at Burghausen in Germany and in Tennessee. Its silicone and chemicals businesses bring in much more revenue than its electronic-grade polysilicon.
aiRelevance: Along with Hemlock and Tokuyama it supplies the feedstock for the wafers used in leading-edge logic and memory.

revenue.basis: Sales, consolidated statement of income, IFRS

name: Tokuyama
role: Japanese chemical maker supplying semiconductor-grade polysilicon from Shunan and Malaysia, plus high-purity isopropyl alcohol and other fab chemicals. It is one of the five major suppliers of electronic-grade silicon that Siltronic names for 2025.
aiRelevance: Polysilicon purity sets the lowest defect density a wafer can reach, which sets the yield on large AI dies.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: OCI Holdings
role: A Korean chemical group that makes polysilicon and fab chemicals, including high-purity hydrogen peroxide and phosphoric acid. Most of its polysilicon goes to solar customers.
aiRelevance: Supplies the bulk wet chemicals Korean memory fabs consume in HBM production.

revenue.basis: 매출액 (Revenue), consolidated, K-IFRS

name: Eswin Material
role: Mainland China's largest maker of 300 mm wafers. It says it ranked sixth in the world with about 7.7 percent of global 300 mm shipments in the first half of 2026, up from about 6 percent in 2024.
aiRelevance: A domestic 300 mm supplier at this scale lets Chinese fabs rely less on the five foreign firms that lead the wafer market.

name: JSR Corporation
ownership: Taken private by the Japan Investment Corporation in 2024
role: A Japanese maker of photoresist, the light-sensitive coating that chip patterns are printed into. It owns Inpria, an Oregon maker of metal-oxide resist for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) printing. A company controlled by the Japan Investment Corporation bought 84.36 percent of its shares in a tender offer that closed on 16 April 2024. Its shares were delisted from the Tokyo Stock Exchange on 25 June 2024.
aiRelevance: EUV resist performance sets the resolution and defect rate of every advanced layer on an AI die.

name: Tokyo Ohka Kogyo
role: Makes photoresist for KrF, ArF immersion and EUV lithography, plus developers, strippers and thick-film resists used in advanced packaging. It has supplied resist since the industry's early days.
aiRelevance: Besides resist for making chips, Tokyo Ohka Kogyo supplies the thick-film resists used to build copper pillars and redistribution layers (fine wiring) in advanced packaging.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: Fujifilm
subcategory: Photoresist, CMP slurry and cleaning chemicals
role: Makes photoresist, developers, CMP polishing slurries, polyimides and cleaning chemicals. It built this large electronic materials business from its photographic film chemistry. Electronic materials are a minority of group revenue but a major share of world supply.
aiRelevance: Supplies both the lithography chemicals for the die and the polyimide dielectrics used in advanced packaging.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, US GAAP

name: Sumitomo Chemical
role: Makes ArF and EUV photoresist and high-purity metals and compounds for fabs, though its petrochemical and agrochemical business is much larger. It is one of the four or five firms with EUV resist that chipmakers have qualified for production.
aiRelevance: EUV resist supply is concentrated in a few Japanese firms, and Sumitomo is one of them.

revenue.basis: Sales revenue (売上収益), consolidated, IFRS

name: Qnity Electronics
subcategory: CMP slurries and pads, lithography and packaging materials
ownership: Public, separated from DuPont on 1 November 2025
role: DuPont's former electronics business, an independent company since 1 November 2025. It supplies chemical mechanical planarization slurries and pads, lithographic materials, and metallization and other materials for chip packaging and circuit boards.
aiRelevance: Every metal layer on an AI die is polished flat with a CMP pad and slurry before the next layer goes down.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Inpria
role: Developed tin-oxide EUV resists that absorb EUV photons far more efficiently than organic chemically amplified resists. Higher absorption cuts the light dose needed and sharpens resolution on High-NA EUV tools.
aiRelevance: Metal-oxide resist is the leading candidate for High-NA EUV layers on future AI logic.

name: Dongjin Semichem
subcategory: Photoresist and thinner for Korean fabs
role: Korea's main domestic photoresist maker, covering i-line, KrF and ArF grades with EUV under development. It expanded after Japan restricted exports of key materials to Korea in 2019.
aiRelevance: Domestic resist supply makes Korean HBM output less exposed to Japanese export policy.

name: Soulbrain
role: Supplies high-purity hydrogen fluoride (HF) etchant, CVD precursors and cleaning chemicals to Korean memory fabs. It localized HF production after the 2019 Japanese export restrictions.
aiRelevance: The etchants that cut the deep, narrow (high aspect ratio) features in DRAM come from a short list of suppliers, and Soulbrain is Korea's.

revenue.basis: 매출액 (Revenue), consolidated, K-IFRS

name: Adeka
role: Makes the organometallic precursor molecules that atomic layer deposition tools use to build films one atomic layer at a time, including metal films and the high-k insulating layers in transistor gates.
aiRelevance: Gate-all-around transistors and DRAM capacitors depend on precursor chemistry as much as on the deposition tool.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: Fujimi Incorporated
nativeName: 株式会社フジミインコーポレーテッド
role: Makes the abrasive slurries used to polish silicon wafers and to planarize (polish flat) the metal and insulating layers built up during chip fabrication. Fujimi tunes each slurry for the process step and the customer.
aiRelevance: Planarization quality limits how many metal layers can be stacked, which matters for dense AI logic and HBM.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: JX Advanced Metals
ownership: Public, listed in Tokyo in 2025 after being spun out of ENEOS
role: Supplies the ultra-high-purity copper, tantalum and titanium sputtering targets used to deposit the metal interconnect on a chip, along with high-purity treated rolled copper foil for substrates.
aiRelevance: Copper purity sets the resistance of the dense wiring on an AI die and how long it lasts before electromigration wears it out. Electromigration is the slow drift of metal atoms pushed by electric current.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, IFRS

name: Merck KGaA
subcategory: Electronic materials, deposition gases and specialty chemicals
role: Its electronics division supplies deposition precursors, specialty gases, CMP slurries and dielectrics. Merck built the division around its acquisitions of Versum Materials and AZ Electronic Materials. It sells one of the broadest ranges of materials of any single supplier.
aiRelevance: Advanced logic and DRAM need hundreds of qualified chemistries, and Merck supplies a large fraction of them.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated income statement, IFRS

name: Entegris
subcategory: Filtration, wafer handling and process chemistries
role: Makes the filters, purifiers, fluid handling components, wafer carriers and specialty coatings that keep contamination out of a fab. It also sells CMP slurries, a business it gained by buying CMC Materials. Fabs use up its products continuously.
aiRelevance: More particles mean more defects, and a large AI die is far more sensitive to defects than a small one.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Linde
ownership: Public. Linde plc, whose predecessor companies Praxair and Linde AG merged in 2018, is incorporated in Ireland, with principal offices in the UK and the US
role: The world's largest industrial gas company. It supplies fabs with nitrogen, hydrogen, helium and rare gases such as the neon used in excimer lasers, usually from plants built next to the fab. Gas supply contracts run for a decade or more.
shareNote: Counted under Germany in the specialty gases country share, a judgment call based on its operating history
aiRelevance: A fab cannot start production without a bulk gas plant. Neon supply for DUV lasers proved fragile after Russia invaded Ukraine.

revenue.basis: Sales, consolidated statements of income, US GAAP

name: Air Liquide
subcategory: Electronic specialty gases and advanced precursors
role: Supplies ultra-pure bulk gases, specialty etch and deposition gases and ALD precursors, with on-site plants at most leading-edge fabs. It also supplies the fluorinated gases used in plasma etch.
aiRelevance: Etch and deposition chemistries for deep, narrow (high aspect ratio) structures depend on a small set of qualified specialty gases.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated income statement, IFRS

name: Air Products
role: Supplies bulk nitrogen, oxygen, hydrogen and helium to fabs through on-site generation, and specialty gases for etch and deposition. It is one of three global suppliers with the scale to serve a gigafab.
aiRelevance: A leading-edge fab uses hundreds of thousands of cubic meters of nitrogen an hour.

revenue.basis: Sales, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Nippon Sanso Holdings
nativeName: 日本酸素ホールディングス
role: The parent of Taiyo Nippon Sanso, supplying bulk and electronic specialty gases in Japan, the US and Asia. It is a major source of the high-purity gases Japanese and Taiwanese fabs consume.
aiRelevance: The fabs and packaging houses that build most AI memory and packages rely on Japanese gas supply.

revenue.basis: Revenue (売上収益), consolidated, IFRS

name: SK Specialty
subcategory: Nitrogen trifluoride and specialty etch gases
ownership: Formerly SK Materials, and SK Inc. sold a majority stake to Hahn & Company
role: Produces nitrogen trifluoride, the gas used to clean deposition chambers, plus tungsten hexafluoride and other specialty etch gases. The more wafers a fab runs through deposition, the more chamber cleaning gas it uses.
aiRelevance: Nitrogen trifluoride (NF3) supply limits how fast deposition chambers can be cleaned and returned to use, and so limits DRAM and 3D NAND flash output.

name: Kanto Denka Kogyo
role: Makes fluorine-based specialty gases including tungsten hexafluoride and carbon fluorides used for plasma etch and chamber cleaning. It is one of a small number of qualified sources for several of these molecules.
aiRelevance: Etching deep, narrow (high aspect ratio) features in DRAM and 3D NAND depends on a small set of fluorinated chemistries.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: Stella Chemifa
role: Refines hydrofluoric acid to the purity needed to etch and clean silicon without leaving metal contamination. Japan's 2019 decision to require export licenses for high-purity HF sent to Korea showed how few qualified sources exist.
aiRelevance: Ultra-pure HF is used at dozens of steps in DRAM manufacture, which makes it a direct input to HBM supply.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: Morita Chemical Industries
subcategory: High-purity hydrogen fluoride and fluorine compounds
role: A Japanese maker of hydrofluoric acid and fluorine compounds. Its electronics grades are used to etch silicon oxide film and to clean semiconductor material.
aiRelevance: Fabs use semiconductor-grade HF to etch and clean wafers, and Morita and Stella Chemifa are two of the Japanese refiners that supply it.

name: Resonac Holdings
subcategory: Etch gases, packaging materials and CMP slurries
role: Supplies high-purity etch gases, CMP slurries, die attach films, and the copper-clad laminates and encapsulants used in advanced packaging. It was formed from Showa Denko and Hitachi Chemical. It leads a consortium on panel-level packaging.
aiRelevance: Its packaging materials go into the CoWoS and fan-out packages that AI accelerators are built in.

revenue.basis: Revenue (売上収益), consolidated, IFRS

name: ASML
role: The only maker of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography scanners, the machines that print circuit patterns onto wafers. It also makes immersion deep ultraviolet (DUV) scanners. Chipmakers use its EUV systems for the most critical layers on the most advanced logic and memory chips.
shareNote: Only manufacturer of EUV lithography systems. Recognized revenue on 48 EUV systems and 279 DUV systems in 2025
aiRelevance: A fab needs EUV to build leading-edge AI logic.

revenue.basis: Total net sales, consolidated statement of profit or loss, EU-IFRS (statutory Annual Report 2025)

name: Nikon
subcategory: ArF immersion, ArF and KrF scanners, i-line steppers, digital lithography
role: Makes ArF immersion, ArF, KrF and i-line lithography systems. It now has a small share of the leading-edge market. But its tools are still used to make chips on older (mature-node) processes, and Nikon services them. Its current lineup includes no EUV system.
aiRelevance: Its tools print some of the chips made on older processes for use around AI systems.

revenue.basis: Revenue (売上収益), consolidated, IFRS

name: Canon
subcategory: i-line and KrF steppers, nanoimprint lithography
role: Makes i-line and KrF steppers for mature nodes and packaging. It is also commercializing nanoimprint lithography, which stamps a pattern into the resist. Nanoimprint needs no EUV optics, but it has defect and throughput limits.
aiRelevance: Canon says its nanoimprint system patterns a minimum linewidth of 14 nm, equivalent to the 5 nm node, without projection optics.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, US GAAP

name: SMEE
ownership: State-owned, backed by the Shanghai municipal government and the National IC Fund
role: A Chinese maker of lithography scanners, founded in 2002 in Shanghai's Zhangjiang park. It ships i-line and KrF class tools for packaging and mature nodes. Reports of a domestic immersion ArF tool in production have not been independently confirmed.
aiRelevance: Until SMEE can ship a production immersion scanner, China's AI logic depends on tools it can no longer import.

name: Cymer
subcategory: DUV excimer light sources and EUV tin plasma sources
role: Builds the light sources for lithography: excimer lasers for DUV scanners and the laser-produced tin plasma source that generates 13.5 nm EUV light. The EUV source is the hardest subsystem in the machine.
aiRelevance: EUV source power sets how many wafers a scanner can expose per hour, and so how much leading-edge AI silicon fabs can print each year.

name: Gigaphoton
nativeName: ギガフォトン株式会社
role: Makes ArF and KrF excimer laser light sources for DUV scanners, including ASML immersion tools. It describes itself as the world's leading excimer laser light source manufacturer. It also offers retrofit sources for installed DUV tools.
aiRelevance: Gigaphoton gives fabs a second source of DUV light, the light used for multipatterning (printing one layer in several exposures) at mature and middle nodes.

name: Carl Zeiss SMT
subcategory: EUV projection optics, illuminators and mask metrology
ownership: Part of the Zeiss Group, with ASML holding a minority stake in Carl Zeiss SMT
role: Makes the multilayer mirrors and projection optics inside every EUV scanner, polished to atomic-scale flatness, plus the larger anamorphic optics for High-NA EUV scanners. Zeiss SMT exclusively supplies the optics for ASML's EUV scanners. It also makes AIMS EUV, which checks how a mask will print under the scanner's own imaging conditions, and MeRiT systems that repair masks.
aiRelevance: The mirror set limits EUV resolution and is the hardest part of the chain to duplicate.

name: Trumpf
subcategory: CO2 drive lasers for EUV sources
role: Builds the multi-kilowatt CO2 laser amplifier chain that vaporizes tin droplets to create EUV light. Trumpf describes the laser system as internationally unique.
aiRelevance: The CO2 laser's power directly sets how much EUV light a scanner gets, and so how many wafers of AI chips it can expose per hour.

name: VDL Groep
role: A Dutch precision manufacturing group that builds large mechanical modules, frames and vacuum assemblies for ASML scanners. It is one of the main suppliers in the Brainport cluster around ASML's base in Veldhoven.
aiRelevance: ASML can ship scanners only as fast as the supply cluster around it builds modules.

name: Jenoptik
role: Supplies precision optics, laser components and optical measurement modules used inside lithography and inspection tools, and makes its own micro-optics.
aiRelevance: Part of the German optics cluster that no other region has reproduced at the same precision.

revenue.basis: Revenue, continuing operations, consolidated statement of profit or loss, IFRS

name: Edwards Vacuum
subcategory: Dry vacuum pumps and abatement systems
role: Supplies the dry pumps that hold process chambers at vacuum and the abatement systems that destroy the toxic and greenhouse gases leaving them. A leading-edge fab runs thousands of pumps continuously.
aiRelevance: Lead times for pumps and abatement systems have limited how fast fabs can bring up new capacity.

name: MKS Instruments
subcategory: RF power, flow control, lasers and plating chemistry
role: Supplies the RF generators, mass flow controllers, pressure gauges, vacuum components and ozone systems inside process tools. Through Atotech it also supplies the electroplating chemistry used for copper interconnect and substrates.
aiRelevance: Hardware that controls plasma processes sets how consistently tools etch and deposit at the dimensions used in AI logic.

revenue.basis: Net revenues, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Advanced Energy Industries
subcategory: Plasma power delivery and precision power
role: Makes the RF and DC power supplies and matching networks that strike and hold the plasmas used in etch and deposition, plus precision power for data-center equipment.
aiRelevance: A stable plasma lets fabs repeat high aspect ratio etch, which cuts deep, narrow holes, with sub-nanometer control.

revenue.basis: Revenue, net, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Ichor Holdings
role: Designs and builds the gas panels, weldments and chemical delivery modules that route process gases into etch and deposition chambers. It is an outsourced manufacturing partner to the large tool vendors.
aiRelevance: Tool vendors cannot ship chambers faster than their subsystem partners can build gas delivery modules.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Ultra Clean Holdings
role: Builds gas delivery systems, chemical modules and frame assemblies for process tools, and runs a large business cleaning and coating chamber parts between uses.
aiRelevance: Chamber parts cleaning is a recurring service, and it determines how much of the time tools can run and how many defects reach the wafer.

revenue.basis: Total revenues, consolidated, US GAAP

name: VAT Group
role: Makes the high-vacuum isolation and control valves that seal and gate every process chamber. How many particles a valve sheds and how many cycles it lasts directly affect tool uptime and wafer defect counts.
shareNote: About 71 percent of the semiconductor and semiconductor-related vacuum valve market (2025)
aiRelevance: VAT supplies most of the valves that every deposition and etch chamber in the world depends on.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated income statement, IFRS

name: Pfeiffer Vacuum
role: Makes turbomolecular pumps, which spin at tens of thousands of revolutions per minute to reach the high vacuum that etch, deposition and EUV chambers require. It also makes leak detection instruments.
aiRelevance: EUV scanners and ion implanters need high vacuum that only turbomolecular pumping can reach.

revenue.basis: Umsatzerlöse (revenue), Konzern-Gewinn- und Verlustrechnung (consolidated income statement), IFRS

name: Horiba
subcategory: Mass flow controllers and in-line analysis
role: Supplies mass flow controllers, which meter process gases into chambers to within a fraction of a percent. It also supplies residual gas analyzers and liquid concentration monitors used across the fab.
aiRelevance: Gas flow accuracy controls how even a film's thickness is across a 300 mm wafer.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: Comet Group
subcategory: RF impedance matching and X-ray inspection
role: Makes RF power delivery components, vacuum capacitors and impedance matching networks for plasma tools, and X-ray systems used to inspect solder joints and packages.
aiRelevance: Very few firms make vacuum capacitors for high-power RF matching, and that supply limits how many plasma etch tools can be built.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated statement of income, IFRS

name: Ferrotec Holdings
nativeName: フェローテックホールディングス
subcategory: Quartz, ceramics, ferrofluidic seals and thermoelectrics
role: Supplies quartz and ceramic chamber consumables, ferrofluidic vacuum feedthroughs, electrostatic chucks and thermoelectric coolers, with much of its manufacturing in China.
aiRelevance: Fabs replace chamber consumables on a schedule, so the supply of consumables limits how much a fab can run.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: Hoya
role: Makes the ultra-flat low-thermal-expansion glass blanks, coated with molybdenum-silicon multilayers, that become EUV photomasks. Hoya says it holds an exceptionally high share of the EUV mask blank market.
aiRelevance: Most EUV layers on an AI accelerator are printed from masks that started as Hoya or AGC blanks.

revenue.basis: Revenue (売上収益), consolidated, IFRS

name: AGC Inc.
subcategory: EUV and DUV mask blanks, synthetic quartz
role: The main supplier of EUV mask blanks besides Hoya, and a major maker of synthetic quartz substrates and photomask glass. AGC says it is the only blank maker that produces EUV blanks in-house from the glass material through the coating. Its glass expertise comes from a much larger architectural and automotive glass business.
aiRelevance: AGC and Hoya are the main sources of the blank under an EUV mask. AGC's EUV blank sales reached ¥40 billion in 2024 and fell in 2025. In June 2026 AGC said sales were recovering and that 2026 demand would exceed 2024's.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, IFRS

name: Photronics
role: A merchant photomask maker, writing and inspecting masks for logic and display customers from plants in the US, Taiwan, Korea, China and Europe. The foundries make most leading-edge masks in-house.
aiRelevance: Merchant mask supply matters most for the mature-node and analog parts around AI systems.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Toppan Holdings
role: Makes advanced photomasks through its photomask arm and is building flip-chip BGA substrate capacity for AI packages. Its photomask business became a separate company, Tekscend Photomask, which is listed in Tokyo.
aiRelevance: Toppan supplies both photomasks and AI package substrates, two of the tighter capacity constraints.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: Dai Nippon Printing
role: Makes photomasks, including EUV masks, plus lead frames and other electronic components. Like Toppan, it applied the precision of commercial printing to semiconductor patterning.
aiRelevance: One of the few merchant sources able to write and repair EUV masks outside the foundries.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: IMS Nanofabrication
ownership: Majority owned by Intel, with Bain Capital and TSMC holding minority stakes
role: Builds the multi-beam electron mask writers that pattern EUV masks with hundreds of thousands of parallel beamlets. On CSET's count it led the market for all electron-beam mask writers in 2025. NuFlare is the only other maker of multi-beam writers.
shareNote: 46.6 percent of the $994 million market for all electron-beam mask writers in 2025, ahead of NuFlare (39.2 percent) and JEOL (14.2 percent), on CSET's analysis of TechInsights data
aiRelevance: Leading-edge EUV masks for AI chips are written on multi-beam tools. In 2023 Intel called IMS the established industry leader in making them.

name: NuFlare Technology
nativeName: 株式会社ニューフレアテクノロジー
role: Makes variable-shaped-beam and multi-beam electron mask writers and mask inspection systems. Its MBM series competes with IMS Nanofabrication in multi-beam mask writing.
aiRelevance: The time it takes to write masks limits how quickly new AI chip designs can reach production.

name: Mitsui Chemicals
role: Supplies EUV pellicles, the thin membranes that keep particles off a photomask while it is exposed. EUV pellicles must transmit over 90 percent of 13.5 nm light and survive high source power. Only a few suppliers make them.
aiRelevance: Without a working pellicle a single particle on a mask repeats as a defect on every AI die printed with it.

revenue.basis: Revenue (売上収益), consolidated, IFRS

name: Shenzhen Qingyi Photomask
subcategory: Merchant photomasks for chips and displays
role: A Chinese merchant mask maker that Photronics names among its competitors in chip and display masks. No Chinese firm makes EUV mask blanks or the tools that check EUV masks.
aiRelevance: Chinese merchant masks cover the mature-node chips around AI systems, but not the EUV layers of an AI die.

name: Shenzhen Newway Photomask
subcategory: Merchant photomasks for chips and displays
role: A Chinese merchant mask maker that Photronics names among its competitors in chip and display masks. No Chinese firm makes EUV mask blanks or the tools that check EUV masks.
aiRelevance: Chinese merchant masks cover the mature-node chips around AI systems, but not the EUV layers of an AI die.

name: KLA
subcategory: Wafer and reticle inspection, process control
role: Supplies process control equipment: optical and electron beam wafer inspection, reticle inspection, overlay and film metrology. Its tools find the defects that determine yield on large dies.
shareNote: 56.8 percent of the process control market in 2025 on CSET's count, against 11.2 percent for Applied Materials, the next largest. Gartner data in KLA's 2026 investor day put it at 56.5 percent in 2024, 6.5 times the nearest competitor.
aiRelevance: A reticle-sized AI die has so much area that a small change in defect density swings yield and cost sharply.

revenue.basis: Total revenues, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Lasertec
nativeName: レーザーテック株式会社
subcategory: EUV mask blank and pattern inspection
role: Makes actinic inspection tools, which use EUV light to inspect EUV mask blanks and patterned masks. Its ACTIS A150 was the world's first actinic EUV patterned mask inspection system. In October 2025 it launched the ACTIS A200HiT series, which it says triples the A150's inspection speed. These tools detect printable phase defects, flaws in a mask's reflective layers that DUV-based mask inspection cannot find.
aiRelevance: EUV masks for AI chips need inspection that can find phase defects. Lasertec built the first actinic tool for patterned masks.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: Hitachi High-Tech
nativeName: 株式会社日立ハイテク
role: The largest supplier of critical dimension scanning electron microscopes (CD-SEMs), which measure feature widths after lithography and etch. It also makes plasma etch systems and electron beam review tools.
aiRelevance: Fabs use CD-SEMs to confirm that an EUV layer printed at the intended dimension before sending the wafer on to the next step.

name: Onto Innovation
subcategory: Optical metrology, inspection and lithography software
role: Supplies optical film metrology, macro defect inspection and packaging inspection, with a strong position in advanced packaging metrology. It was formed from Rudolph Technologies and Nanometrics.
aiRelevance: Advanced packaging inspection has become a bottleneck as AI packages grow past 100 mm on a side.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Nova Ltd
role: Supplies optical critical dimension scatterometry and X-ray metrology used to measure three-dimensional structures such as gate-all-around nanosheets and high aspect ratio memory holes.
aiRelevance: Fabs cannot control the gate-all-around process without measuring the dimensions of buried structures.

revenue.basis: Total revenues, consolidated statements of operations, US GAAP

name: Camtek
role: Makes inspection and metrology systems for bumping, wafer-level packaging and HBM assembly, including tools that measure bump height and coplanarity across a wafer.
aiRelevance: HBM stacking and CoWoS assembly need per-bump inspection because a single bad joint scraps an expensive package.

revenue.basis: Revenues, consolidated statements of income, US GAAP

name: Park Systems
role: Makes the automated atomic force microscopes fabs use to measure surface roughness, step height and defect profiles at sub-nanometer resolution. It acquired the ellipsometry maker Accurion in 2022 and the holographic microscopy maker Lyncée Tec in 2025.
aiRelevance: Hybrid bonding joins two wafers atom to atom, so their surfaces need sub-nanometer control.

revenue.basis: 수익(매출액) (Revenue), consolidated, K-IFRS

name: Skyverse Technology
subcategory: Domestic Chinese wafer inspection and metrology
ownership: Public (Shanghai STAR Market), with state-backed investors
role: A Shenzhen maker of wafer defect inspection and film metrology tools, aiming to replace KLA systems in Chinese fabs. Its coverage is strongest at mature nodes.
shareNote: 2,053,298,171.74 yuan of revenue in 2025, up 48.75 percent on 2024, per its 2025 annual report summary.
aiRelevance: CSET counts Chinese makers at 0.7 percent of process control tools in 2025.

name: Wuhan Jingce Electronic
subcategory: Domestic Chinese metrology and display test
role: Makes semiconductor film metrology, electrical test and defect inspection tools for Chinese fabs through its Wuhan Jingce Semiconductor arm. It started in flat panel display test.
aiRelevance: Wuhan Jingce is part of China's effort to make its own process control tools.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Applied Materials
subcategory: Deposition, epitaxy, CMP, implant and e-beam metrology
role: Makes tools for physical and chemical vapor deposition, epitaxy, ion implantation, chemical mechanical planarization and electron beam inspection. Its tools cover more process steps than any other vendor's.
aiRelevance: Gate-all-around transistors and advanced interconnect need dozens of Applied deposition steps per wafer.

revenue.basis: Net revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Lam Research
subcategory: Plasma etch, deposition and wafer clean
role: The largest supplier of plasma etch systems. According to CSET, it had 41.1 percent of the $21.9 billion dry etch tool market in 2025, against 23.4 percent for Tokyo Electron. Its line includes the high aspect ratio etch used to drill 3D NAND channels and DRAM capacitors, plus atomic layer deposition, electroplating and cryogenic etch tools.
aiRelevance: HBM depends on deep silicon vias and dense DRAM capacitors, and Lam makes etch tools for both.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Tokyo Electron
nativeName: 東京エレクトロン株式会社
subcategory: Coater/developer track, etch, deposition and clean
role: Makes the coater/developer track, which applies photoresist, develops it after exposure and is physically linked to every scanner in a fab. It also makes etch, deposition, cleaning and wafer bonding systems, and wafer probers for chip testing.
shareNote: 91 percent of the world coater/developer (track) market in CY2025, on Gartner data published in Tokyo Electron's own results presentation
aiRelevance: Tokyo Electron holds more than 90 percent of the coater/developer market. That share makes the track linked to each scanner as hard a dependency as the scanner.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, J-GAAP

name: ASM International
role: Makes atomic layer deposition (ALD) tools, which grow films one atomic layer at a time. Chipmakers use ALD to build gate-all-around transistors and high-k dielectrics. ASM also makes epitaxy and plasma-enhanced ALD tools.
aiRelevance: ALD defines the structure of the gate-all-around nanosheet transistors in TSMC N2 and Intel 18A class logic.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statement of profit or loss, IFRS (EU)

name: Kokusai Electric
ownership: Public, listed in Tokyo in 2023 after KKR ownership
role: Makes batch vertical furnaces and batch ALD systems that process dozens of wafers at once. Memory makers use them widely for DRAM and 3D NAND film steps where throughput matters more than single-wafer control.
aiRelevance: How fast batch tools deposit films directly affects how many DRAM wafers, and so how many HBM stacks, fabs can produce.

revenue.basis: Revenue (売上収益), consolidated, IFRS

name: Naura Technology
subcategory: Etch, deposition, clean and furnace systems
ownership: Public (Shenzhen), state-backed, with the National IC Fund as an investor
role: China's largest semiconductor equipment maker, with plasma etch, deposition (PVD, CVD and ALD), furnace and cleaning tools. As Chinese fabs replaced foreign tools with local ones, Naura rose into the world's top ten chipmaking equipment suppliers by sales in 2025. That year three Chinese firms made the global top 20, up from one in 2022.
aiRelevance: Naura is the clearest measure of how far China has come in replacing American and Japanese process tools.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: AMEC
role: Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment makes capacitively and inductively coupled plasma etch systems used at Chinese logic and memory fabs, plus MOCVD reactors for LEDs. Its etchers are the most competitive Chinese tools at advanced nodes.
aiRelevance: Etch is the step where Chinese equipment has come closest to parity with foreign tools.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: Piotech
role: China's main domestic supplier of plasma-enhanced CVD and ALD systems, and more recently hybrid wafer bonding tools aimed at 3D integration.
aiRelevance: Any Chinese attempt to make HBM at home needs deposition and bonding tools.

revenue.basis: 营业收入 (operating revenue), consolidated income statement (合并利润表), China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (企业会计准则); table unit 元 (yuan)

name: SCREEN Holdings
nativeName: 株式会社SCREENホールディングス
role: Makes the single-wafer and batch cleaning systems that remove particles and residues between almost every process step. Cleaning is the most frequently repeated operation in a fab.
aiRelevance: Defects left by cleaning add up across hundreds of steps and show up as yield loss on large AI dies.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), consolidated, J-GAAP

name: SEMES
role: Supplies wafer cleaning, coater/developer track, etch and packaging systems, mainly to Samsung. By its own description it is Korea's largest maker of chip and display equipment, with sales of about KRW 2.46 trillion in 2025. Through SEMES, Samsung keeps some tool technology in house.
aiRelevance: Supplies a meaningful share of the tools inside the fabs that make most of the world's HBM.

name: ACM Research
subcategory: Wafer cleaning, plating and packaging tools
ownership: Public, with principal operations through ACM Research Shanghai
role: Makes single-wafer cleaning systems using megasonic and bubble technologies, plus electroplating and advanced packaging tools. It is US-listed but manufactures and sells largely in China.
aiRelevance: Cleaning is one of the segments where Chinese fabs have found a workable non-Japanese supplier.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: TSMC
subcategory: Leading-edge logic foundry and advanced packaging
ownership: Public, with the Taiwanese state holding a minority stake
role: Manufactures almost every leading-edge AI accelerator, including those of Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom and the custom chips of large cloud companies, on its N4, N3 and N2 processes. It also owns CoWoS and SoIC advanced packaging, and its packaging capacity is a tighter constraint than its wafer capacity.
aiRelevance: TSMC is the single most concentrated point in the AI chain, because it both makes and packages the dies, mostly in Taiwan.

revenue.basis: Net revenue, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: Samsung Foundry
role: A foundry running its 2 nm class SF2 process in Korea and building a fab in Taylor, Texas. Its gate-all-around transistors, introduced at 3 nm, are in production. Large AI customers keep qualifying it as a second source.
aiRelevance: A credible second leading-edge foundry is the main hedge against the concentration of leading-edge production in Taiwan.

name: Intel Foundry
ownership: Division of Intel Corporation, in which the US government took an equity stake in 2025
role: Intel's manufacturing arm, running the 18A process with RibbonFET gate-all-around and PowerVia backside power, plus EMIB and Foveros packaging. Most of its output is still Intel's own chips. Outside customers provided only $293 million of its $5.765 billion of segment revenue in the quarter to 27 June 2026.
aiRelevance: 18A gives AI chip designers a leading-edge process from a US-owned foundry on US soil, and 14A will too once Intel completes its development.

name: SMIC
ownership: Public (Hong Kong and Shanghai), state-backed, with the National IC Fund as an investor
role: China's largest foundry, producing 7 nm class logic using multipatterning on immersion DUV because it cannot buy EUV. CSET reported in June 2024 that Huawei's Ascend 910B AI chip is believed to be made on its N+2 process. But SemiAnalysis judged in April 2025 that most 910B and 910C chips were made at TSMC. It is on the US Entity List.
aiRelevance: SMIC's yield and capacity at 7 nm cap how many Chinese AI accelerators can be made at home.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statement of profit or loss, IFRS Accounting Standards; table in USD thousands

name: Hua Hong Semiconductor
role: A foundry focused on mature-node specialty processes, including power management, embedded memory and analog. It is mainland China's second largest pure-play foundry and the world's fifth largest by 2025 sales. It does not make leading-edge logic.
aiRelevance: Supplies the power management and analog parts that surround AI processors.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statement of profit or loss, HKFRS Accounting Standards; table in US$ thousands

name: GlobalFoundries
ownership: Public, with Mubadala of Abu Dhabi as the largest shareholder
role: Runs mature and specialty processes for RF, automotive, power and silicon photonics from fabs in New York, Vermont, Germany and Singapore. It stopped developing leading-edge processes in 2018.

ownership: Public, incorporated in the Cayman Islands with operations in Thailand
role: A contract manufacturer of optical modules and photonic assemblies, building transceivers and optical engines for the largest networking and AI vendors from plants in Thailand.
aiRelevance: A large share of the world's AI-cluster optics is assembled in a small number of buildings in Thailand.

revenue.basis: Revenues, consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income, US GAAP

name: Ayar Labs
ownership: Private, with investors including Nvidia, Intel Capital and AMD
role: Builds optical input and output chiplets that put light directly into the processor package, replacing electrical SerDes with fiber at the package edge.
aiRelevance: Optical I/O is the leading proposal for scaling accelerator bandwidth beyond what copper can carry.

name: Lightmatter
role: Develops photonic interposers and optical interconnect that route light beneath stacked dies, aiming to remove the bandwidth limit between accelerators in a package.
customers: Research and hyperscale partners under development
aiRelevance: Photonic interposers would change the scaling limits of multi-die AI packages if they reach production.

name: Corning
subcategory: Optical fiber, cable and glass substrates
role: Makes the optical fiber and cabling that connect data center halls and campuses, and develops glass substrates for semiconductor packaging. It also holds the majority stake in Hemlock Semiconductor.
aiRelevance: Scaling out an AI cluster requires fiber inside and between campuses.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, US GAAP

name: AXT
subcategory: Indium phosphide and gallium arsenide substrates
role: Makes the indium phosphide wafers that lasers for optical links are grown on. It is listed in the US but does all its manufacturing in China. China has required export permits for indium phosphide substrates since February 2025. In its filing for the quarter to June 2026, AXT called the permits the most significant challenge it faces.
aiRelevance: Laser makers need indium phosphide wafers, and AXT makes them only in China, so it depends on Chinese export permits.

name: Hon Hai Precision
role: Builds Nvidia servers and rack-scale systems, with assembly in Taiwan, Mexico, the US and Southeast Asia. It is the largest electronics contract manufacturer and the world's largest AI server provider.
aiRelevance: A handful of Taiwanese firms assemble and burn in rack-scale AI systems, and Hon Hai (Foxconn) is the largest of them.

revenue.basis: Operating revenue, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: Quanta Computer
role: Builds GPU baseboards, servers and full racks for hyperscalers and for Nvidia reference systems, with plants in Taiwan, the US, Mexico and Thailand. It is one of the largest AI server ODMs, the contract firms that design and build servers for other companies.
aiRelevance: Quanta and its peers turn accelerators into racks ready to deploy, and their capacity limits how fast AI hardware goes into service.

revenue.basis: Operating revenue, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: Wistron
subcategory: AI server and GPU baseboard manufacturing
role: Builds GPU baseboards and AI servers, and grew quickly during the 2025 AI build-out. It also supplies liquid cooling loops and rack integration.
aiRelevance: GPU baseboard assembly is a specialized step with few qualified suppliers worldwide.

revenue.basis: Net revenues, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: Wiwynn
role: Designs and builds hyperscale servers, storage and rack systems to Open Compute designs for cloud operators, including liquid-cooled AI racks.
aiRelevance: Hyperscalers use Open Compute rack designs to deploy AI capacity built to their own specifications.

revenue.basis: Operating revenue, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: Inventec
role: Builds AI and general purpose servers for cloud operators and OEMs, with manufacturing in Taiwan, Mexico, the Czech Republic and Malaysia.
aiRelevance: One of the Taiwanese ODMs that build AI servers for cloud operators.

revenue.basis: Operating revenue, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: Super Micro Computer
role: Designs and builds AI servers and complete liquid-cooled racks, with final assembly in California, Taiwan and Malaysia. It was among the first to ship direct-to-chip liquid cooling at volume.
aiRelevance: One of the few US-based firms that integrate AI racks in-house.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Dell Technologies
role: Sells PowerEdge AI servers and integrated rack systems to enterprises and AI cloud operators, adding services, financing and deployment on top of the hardware.
aiRelevance: Enterprises mostly buy their AI hardware from the large server OEMs.

revenue.basis: Total net revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
role: Builds AI servers and Cray supercomputers with direct liquid cooling, and since acquiring Juniper Networks also supplies data center networking.
aiRelevance: HPE's liquid cooling and interconnect experience from Cray applies directly to dense AI clusters.

revenue.basis: Total net revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Lenovo
role: Builds AI servers and its Neptune warm-water liquid cooling systems, selling into enterprises and research computing worldwide from plants in China, Hungary, Mexico and the US.
aiRelevance: Warm-water cooling avoids chillers entirely, which matters as rack power passes 100 kW.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated income statement, HKFRS Accounting Standards; table in US$ thousands

name: ZT Systems
ownership: Acquired by AMD in 2025, and AMD sold the manufacturing operation on to Sanmina
role: Designs and validates rack-scale AI systems for hyperscalers. AMD bought it for its systems engineering team, so that AMD could ship complete racks.
aiRelevance: Competing with Nvidia now requires shipping an integrated rack.

name: Celestica
role: Builds servers, storage and 800G Ethernet switches for hyperscalers on a contract basis, and has grown strongly with AI networking demand.
aiRelevance: Contract manufacturers such as Celestica build a significant share of AI back-end switch hardware.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statement of operations, US GAAP

name: Jabil
subcategory: Contract manufacturing and liquid cooling hardware
role: A large contract manufacturer building AI data center hardware including server racks, power distribution and liquid cooling components such as cold plates and manifolds.
aiRelevance: Cold plate and manifold manufacturing has become a capacity constraint for liquid-cooled racks.

revenue.basis: Net revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Vertiv
subcategory: Data center power and thermal management
role: Makes uninterruptible power supplies, busway power distribution, coolant distribution units and liquid cooling systems for data centers. It co-develops reference power and cooling designs with Nvidia.
aiRelevance: A 132 kW rack cannot be air cooled, so it needs a coolant distribution unit to pump liquid through its servers.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Schneider Electric
role: Supplies medium and low voltage electrical distribution, uninterruptible power supplies under the APC brand, busway and liquid cooling for data centers, plus the design software operators plan with.
aiRelevance: AI data center schedules now depend on lead times for electrical equipment, especially transformers and switchgear.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statement of income, IFRS

name: Eaton
role: Makes switchgear, busway, transformers, UPS systems and power distribution units for data centers, a segment that has become supply constrained as AI campuses scale.
aiRelevance: A grid connection and on-site electrical gear now take longer to obtain than the GPUs themselves.

revenue.basis: Net sales, consolidated statements of income, US GAAP

name: Delta Electronics
subcategory: Power supplies, power shelves and thermal systems
role: A global leader in switching power supplies and a maker of the power shelves and busbars used in AI racks, plus fans, cold plates and coolant distribution units. It supplies equipment for the 800-volt DC power architecture that Nvidia has moved toward.
aiRelevance: A small number of Taiwanese suppliers dominate efficient power conversion for racks of 100 kW and above.

revenue.basis: Operating revenue, consolidated, Taiwan-IFRS (IFRSs as endorsed by the FSC)

name: CoolIT Systems
role: Makes direct-to-chip liquid cooling cold plates, coolant distribution units and manifolds for servers, and is one of the specialists the server ODMs buy from.
aiRelevance: Cold plate design and supply is its own bottleneck, separate from server supply.

name: Asetek
role: Developed direct-to-chip liquid cooling for servers and high performance computing, licensing and supplying pumps, cold plates and rack coolant distribution units.
aiRelevance: An early liquid cooling specialist, in a market that became mainstream as AI racks grew denser.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statement of comprehensive income, IFRS (EU)

name: Hitachi Energy
ownership: Subsidiary of Hitachi (formerly ABB Power Grids)
role: Makes the high voltage transformers, switchgear and grid connection equipment that data center campuses need to draw hundreds of megawatts. Transformer lead times run to several years.
aiRelevance: Large power transformers take longer to deliver than any other physical item between a chip order and a running cluster.

name: Siemens Energy
role: Supplies gas turbines, grid transmission equipment and transformers. Its orders are booked years ahead because data center and electrification demand exceeds its manufacturing capacity.
aiRelevance: The AI buildout now includes new generating capacity, both on site and on the grid.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statements of income, IFRS

name: GE Vernova
subcategory: Gas turbines, grid equipment including transformers, and generation
role: Builds gas turbines, grid equipment and wind turbines. It is a main supplier of the new generating capacity being contracted specifically to power AI data centers. It bought the remaining half of the transformer maker Prolec GE in the first half of 2026.
aiRelevance: Turbine delivery slots have become a limiting factor for new AI campuses in the United States.

revenue.basis: Total revenues, consolidated and combined, US GAAP

name: Monolithic Power Systems
role: Makes the multiphase voltage regulator and power module chips that convert 12 or 48 volts down to the sub-one-volt rails an accelerator core needs, at currents above 1,000 amperes.
aiRelevance: Delivering a thousand amperes into a die at a controlled voltage is one of the hardest board-level problems in AI hardware.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated, US GAAP

name: Infineon
role: Supplies the MOSFETs, gallium nitride devices and power stages used from the grid connection through the rack power shelf to the point-of-load regulator. It is the largest power semiconductor maker, according to Omdia figures Infineon published in August 2026. Those figures give it 17.3 percent of the $32.5 billion market for power discretes and modules in 2025, against 7.2 percent for onsemi.
aiRelevance: Nvidia's move to 800-volt DC rack power distribution depends on power semiconductors from a handful of suppliers.

revenue.basis: Revenue, consolidated statement of profit or loss, IFRS

name: Nidec
role: Makes precision motors, high static pressure server fans, pumps and liquid cooling modules, and supplies the coolant distribution hardware used in dense AI racks.
aiRelevance: Liquid-cooled racks still need fans and pumps, and motor supply is concentrated in a few Japanese firms.

revenue.basis: Net sales (売上高), continuing operations, consolidated, IFRS
revenue.note: Nidec's auditor gave no opinion on these accounts, a disclaimer of opinion in the report filed on 30 September 2026.

name: Mitsubishi Power
subcategory: Gas turbines and power generation equipment
role: Makes gas turbines from the 30 MW class to the 563 MW class. It is the power systems brand of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. In its 2025 annual report, GE Vernova names Mitsubishi Power and Siemens Energy among the key competitors of its power generation business.
aiRelevance: Gas turbines are one of the ways new AI campuses get power, and only a few firms build the largest ones.
